page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.13xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual machine within the Enhanced family, built on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 52 dedicated vCPUs running on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a compute-dense memory ratio of approximately 1.85 GB per vCPU. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included with this instance type.

The storage and network profiles are tailored toward distributed, network-reliant environments. The instance does not feature local disk storage, necessitating external cloud block storage for persistent data requirements. To support data transfer between external storage volumes and distributed services, the ecs.c6t.13xlarge provides a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps without bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

With its low memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated core model, the ecs.c6t.13xlarge offers predictable compute execution without per-core memory overhead. This hardware allocation profile makes it appropriate for distributed compilation, batch compute pipelines, continuous integration runners, and high-concurrency microservice architectures.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6t.13xlarge is a compute-optimized instance from the Enhanced family, designed for high-density processing workloads. It features 52 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM. This configuration provides a compute-heavy memory-to-core allocation of roughly 1.85 GB per vCPU. The instance operates without integrated local storage or hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage while offering a 16 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The substantial core count and dedicated CPU execution environment make this server particularly effective for highly parallelized computation, large-scale batch processing, distributed compilation, and CPU-intensive containerized services that do not require extensive per-core memory capacities.
